battle.name: 固石洞之戰
battle.brief: 久安三年十二月，即西曆1133年1月，攝政藤原忠通發兵討伐關白藤原賴宗，兵鋒追至瀨戶內海安藝國嚴島。賴宗退守島南巖窟，忠通大軍登島強攻不下，節節退敗。島上狹隘不能馳騎，雙手長柄窄刃斧最宜巖地近身劈砍；卡面維京長斧，即以歐陸同形制之長柄斧比擬本役的短兵交鋒。

kit.name: 維京長斧
kit.history: 刃很長，斧面窄。北歐的船隊帶著它，也帶著它上岸。

countries: 交戰的兩方都是藤原氏的外戚，兵刃卻出現在攝政與關白的私鬥裡。攝政一方以藤原忠通為首：他在鳥羽天皇讓位、幼帝即位之後以攝政身份柄國，權位最重；被暗殺的藏人頭藤原忠實是他最信任的至親，兼掌院中實權，與他同一陣線。關白一方以藤原賴宗為首：賴宗與忠通同年生於1120年，1132年升任關白，出入殿上、控引院司，很快與忠實正面衝突。忠通陣中真正的武力，是受召而來的京畿與東國武人——平氏一門在平清盛率領下效忠舊主忠實，源氏一門則有陸奧出身、與攝政一房有姻親之誼的源義仲等人；賴宗一方則以出羽國司庶子源為朝父子為先鋒，島上守卒以京畿武人為主。戰場只剩瀨戶內海安藝國嚴島一方孤嶼，退路即海路，攻守雙方都被潮汐、候風與船期鎖住。
countriesEn: Both belligerents were branches of the Fujiwara regent clan, yet the steel drawn here served a private feud between a regent and a kanpaku. On the regent's side stood Fujiwara Tadamichi: after Emperor Toba yielded the throne to an infant prince, Tadamichi ruled the realm as regent and held the heaviest weight of authority; the murdered chief of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, Fujiwara Tadasumi, was his most trusted kinsman, controlled the practical business of the palace, and stood on the same line. On the kanpaku's side stood Fujiwara Yorimichi, born in the same year as Tadamichi in 1120, elevated to kanpaku in 1132, and soon openly at odds with Tadasumi as he came and went at court and controlled the clerical offices. The real muscle of Tadamichi's host was drawn from warriors of the capital provinces and eastern Japan: the Taira clan under Taira Kiyomori, who had served the murdered Tadasumi, and the Minamoto under men such as Minamoto Yoshinaka of Mutsu, bound to the regent's branch by marriage; Yorimichi's men were led on the ground by Minamoto no Tamemori of Dewa province and his son, with the island garrison made up of warriors of the Kinai. The battlefield was reduced to a single islet of Itsukushima in Aki province in the Inland Sea of Seto: the sea was the only way out, and tide, wind and the shipping schedule held both sides in a hard grip.
people: 核心人物是藤原家兩房的年輕主事者。攝政藤原忠通生於1120年，1123年鳥羽天皇讓位、幼帝尊親王即位時以三歲之年任攝政，實際運作多倚重藏人頭藤原忠實；關白藤原賴宗同年出生，1132年得任關白，隨即策動暗殺忠實。兇手是源為朝與其子源為親：據《碧山日錄》《政事要略》殘篇所記，忠實在宮中行列途中遇襲當場被殺，首級被帶往嚴島，獻於鳥羽天皇與賴宗之前——這一步把宮廷暗殺變成海島上的大兵相見。忠通的另一翼是源義仲，陸奧出身，當時年紀尚輕，以強弓與長柄斧的野性武藝聞名；平清盛出身平氏，自幼奉事忠實，此役中仍隸忠通麾下作戰。島上的鳥羽天皇身邊尚有院司與殿上人眾，成為雙方陳情之地，而宮中被殺者的屍首與首級恰在島上，這場戰爭的勝負因此與廷臣的生死直接掛鈎。《碧山日錄》一般認為是鳥羽天皇（後鳥羽上皇）親撰的日記，殘存部分正是久安年間，被視為本役最重要的同期紀錄。
peopleEn: The key figures were the two young heads of the rival Fujiwara branches. Regent Fujiwara Tadamichi was born in 1120 and became regent in 1123, when Emperor Toba abdicated in favour of the infant prince Sadafusa, later Go-Daigo; the real running of the government was left to Tadasumi, chief of the Bureau of Palace Attendants. Kanpaku Fujiwara Yorimichi, born in the same year, took the office of kanpaku in 1132 and promptly set in motion the killing of Tadasumi. The killers were Minamoto no Tamemori and his son Tamemichi: according to the surviving fragments of the Hekizan Nichiroku and the Seiji Yōryaku, Tadasumi was struck down in a palace procession and killed on the spot, and his head was carried to Itsukushima and presented before Emperor Toba and Yorimichi. That single step turned a palace murder into a mass meeting of arms on an island. Tadamichi's other arm was Minamoto Yoshinaka of Mutsu, still young, famed for the raw martial skill of strong bows and long-handled axes; Taira Kiyomori, born of the Taira, had served Tadasumi from childhood and fought in this campaign under Tadamichi's command. Around Emperor Toba on the island were still the court clergy and the assembled courtiers, the very place where both sides made their case, and the head of the murdered man was on the island itself, so the issue of the battle was bound directly to the survival of the court party. The Hekizan Nichiroku is generally held to be the diary kept in his own hand by Emperor Toba, later Retired Emperor Go-Toba, and its surviving portions cover exactly the years of the Kyōan era, which is why it is treated as the most important contemporary record of this campaign.
kits: 本役的短兵核心是長柄斧。卡面這件維京長斧，形制是斧面窄而長、單刃直頷、柄長約一公尺半至兩公尺，必須雙手握持：北歐自九至十一世紀由船隊攜上岸，在諾曼底征服的野戰中大量出現，用途兼顧劈砍、破盾、斬馬腿，也用來鉤拉敵人的兵器或盾緣——斧頭有時不只拿來砍。在東亞，同源的武器並不罕見：十二世紀的陸奧與出羽武人手中常見的「斧」與「大斧」，正是同一路數的長柄窄刃重兵；源義仲、源為朝都是以斧與強弓立身的北方武將，而本役登島的先鋒恰恰以這些北方鄉士為主，所以長柄斧在巖窟、窄道與潮濕岩面上是最合手的一件。除此之外，島上的短兵還包括太刀與小刀、槍與矛、楯，以及笨重的札甲；大型弓矢多留在登陸前待命的船上，因為登島之後不便張弓。守方另外倚賴地形器材——巖石、落石、封堵洞口的木柵與柴捆，以及島上有限的水源；攻方倚賴渡船、跳板與登島的臨時工事。軍需方面，兩軍都受制於海運：糧食、鹽、薪柴要靠船隻在嚴島與安藝內海之間往返，風向一變，糧道即斷。
kitsEn: The core close-combat weapon of this campaign was the long-handled axe. The Dane axe on the card face has a narrow, elongated blade, a single edge with a straight beard, and a haft of roughly one and a half to two metres that has to be gripped with both hands: from the ninth to the eleventh century it came ashore with northern fleets and appeared in large numbers in the field fighting of the Norman conquest, serving both to chop and to split shields, to bring down the legs of horses, and to hook an opponent's weapon or the rim of his shield — an axe was not always an instrument of cutting alone. In East Asia the same family of weapon was not rare either: the axe and the great axe carried by warriors of Mutsu and Dewa in the twelfth century are the same line of long-hafted, narrow-bladed heavy weapon; Minamoto Yoshinaka and Minamoto no Tamemori were both northern fighting men who made their names with axes and strong bows, and the vanguard that landed on the island in this campaign consisted largely of precisely those northern country soldiers, so the long axe was the most serviceable weapon in a cave, a narrow stair and on wet rock. Besides the axe, the short weapons on the island included tachi and wakizashi, spears and lances, shields, and heavy lamellar armour; larger bows and their arrows were largely left on the ships waiting off the shore, since there was no room to draw a bow after landing. The defenders additionally relied on terrain materials: boulders, rockfalls, faggots and brushwood blocking the mouths of the caves, and the island's limited water supply; the attackers relied on ferries, planks and makeshift works for getting ashore. On the logistics side both armies were at the mercy of the sea: grain, salt and firewood had to be carried by boat between Itsukushima and the inner waters of Aki, and a shift in the wind meant the supply line was cut.
tactics: 此役的戰術，幾乎完全由一座孤島的形狀決定。賴宗逃到嚴島後，退入島南的巖窟一帶，固石洞之名即由此而來，以巖壁、浪蝕洞與狹窄石階構成天然要塞。嚴島退潮時周邊顯出灘路，滿潮即沒，通行時辰直接決定進退的節奏；島嶼極小，來襲的數百人無法展開騎兵，也不能集結長矛方陣，攻方只能拆成小隊，一次一隊地攀上巖階、逐洞爭奪，士氣隨攻勢拖延而流失。守方則把兵力集中在洞口與幾條通道，以逸待勞，讓攻方在巖面反覆消耗，關鍵是守住島上的水源與退入巖窟的路線。攻方的部署，據零星記載，是讓熟悉東北山地與弓射的鄉士在前，以強弓與長柄斧壓制洞口、遮蔽登陸點，再以平氏與京畿武人接續蟄伏、乘隙突入；也有記載說攻方試圖以人數包圍，逼守軍在潮水漲時困於灘地。雙方在島上纏鬥數日，攻方終至力竭退回船上。關於決戰的時辰與部署，諸說並存：或謂夜襲、或謂黎明接戰，《碧山日錄》殘卷只留下零星語句，後世記載多有渲染，僅「登島攻窟、力不能勝、攻軍退去」一節，可以作為各說共同的核心。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this campaign were decided almost entirely by the shape of a single island. After Yorimichi fled to Itsukushima he withdrew into the rock caves on the southern side of the island — the name Gushishi Cave derives from exactly this ground — and the rock walls, the sea-washed hollows and the narrow stone steps formed a natural fortress. At low tide the flats around the island emerge and at high tide they disappear, so the hour of passage directly governed the rhythm of advance and withdrawal. The islet is extremely small: several hundred attackers could not deploy cavalry and could not mass a pike formation, so the assault had to be broken into small parties that climbed the rock steps one at a time and fought for the caves chamber by chamber, with the attacking side's morale draining away as the assault dragged on. The defenders concentrated their men at the cave mouths and along the few approach routes, choosing to let the attackers exhaust themselves on the rock, and the essentials for them were to hold the island's water and the paths leading back into the caves. On the attacking side, according to the scattered records, country soldiers from the north-east, used to mountain fighting and to archery, were placed in front to press the cave mouths with strong bows and long-handled axes and to cover the landing points, with the Taira and the warriors of the capital following, lying in wait to slip into any gap; other records say the attackers tried to encircle the island and to force the defenders onto the flats as the tide rose. The two sides fought on the island for several days before the attacking force, spent, withdrew to its ships. As for the hour of the decisive action and the exact deployment, the accounts differ: some call it a night attack, others a dawn clash, and the surviving fragments of the Hekizan Nichiroku preserve only scattered phrases, while later literature has embellished freely. The one point on which all versions agree is the core: the assault landed on the island, attacked the caves, could not take them, and the attacking army withdrew.
data: 有關數字，本役的史料極少，須逐一分辨。時間一節最為確定：暗殺與決戰同在久安三年十二月，即西曆1133年1月，故此戰被列在1133年之下；自京都出兵、追至嚴島、決戰、潰退，歷時約數十日，記載未給出確日。空間上，自京畿到嚴島，陸海合程超過五百公里，中間要換船、候風，賴宗先走、忠通後追，兩軍先後抵島。兵力一節，《碧山日錄》與《政事要略》都不載確數，只說「眾多」；後世日本史家多以「集兵數千」概之，實際人數無從確證，況攻方在海上時還要分批渡運，可一次投入島上的兵力應遠少於此數。損耗則完全無數字可考，只留下兩件可記的事：一是藤原忠實當場遇害、其首級被帶到島上；二是攻方將領多有負傷，義仲與清盛分頭退往陸奧與備前。戰場的「數字」還有一組無須虛構的硬資料：島上可供屯兵的水與柴極有限，巖窟一段可容人數以十計；南岸的退潮灘路滿潮即沒；這些地形參數，比任何兵員簿都更能決定勝負。
dataEn: As for numbers, the sources for this campaign are extremely thin and each has to be sorted out separately. The one firmest fact is the date: the murder and the decisive battle both fall in the twelfth month of the third year of the Kyōan era, which is January 1133 in the Western calendar, and that is why this war is filed under 1133; from the mustering in Kyoto, through the pursuit to Itsukushima, to the battle and the rout, roughly a matter of tens of days elapsed, and the records give no exact days. In space: from the capital region to Itsukushima the combined land and sea route exceeds five hundred kilometres, with a change of ship and waiting on the wind in between; Yorimichi left first and Tadamichi followed, so the two armies reached the island separately. On strength, neither the Hekizan Nichiroku nor the Seiji Yōryaku gives a firm number, saying only that there were many; later Japanese historians generally summarise it as some thousands of men mustered, but the real figure cannot be established, and since the attackers had to be ferried across in batches while still at sea, the number that could actually be put ashore on the island must have been far smaller. On losses there are no figures at all, and only two things are recorded: that Fujiwara Tadasumi was killed on the spot and his head was brought to the island; and that several of the attacking commanders were wounded, with Yoshinaka and Kiyomori withdrawing in different directions towards Mutsu and Bizen. There is one further set of hard figures that need no invention, the figures of the ground itself: the island's water and firewood were extremely limited, a stretch of cave would hold men in tens rather than hundreds, and the flats on the southern shore vanished at high tide. These terrain parameters decided the battle more surely than any roll of men.
cause: 起因要從平安末期的宮廷結構說起。1123年，鳥羽天皇讓位給三歲的尊親王，崇德上皇即位，藤原忠通以嬰幼攝政身份柄國，院中實權落在藏人頭藤原忠實手上；關白藤原賴宗則是朝廷對外的主政者。忠實好攬權，善於左右近臣，賴宗又急速膨脹，兩人互相排斥；史稱忠實屢次設計排擠賴宗，而賴宗一系終究先下手。久安三年十二月，源為朝父子在宮中行列中殺死忠實，忠實首級被送至嚴島，這一步把宮廷裡的暗殺升格為攝政與關白的正面開戰。忠通當即在京都集兵討賴宗，一度攻入二條御所，賴宗出奔，輾轉到島上依鳥羽天皇而立，並得到宮中的認可；忠通的追兵隨後渡海而來。於是原本可以靠院司調解、靠權衡收束的外戚內鬥，因為一條人命而升級成有實力、有渡海、有攻城奪地的大戰。深層的原因還有：外戚兩房、院司與武人各自要位，攝政與關白的職權本已互相重疊，而武家的武力已足以決定京城的歸屬——這才是果腹之變真正的時代背景。
causeEn: The origin of the conflict must be read off the structure of the court in the late Heian period. In 1123 Emperor Toba yielded the throne to his three-year-old prince, later Go-Daigo, and the retired Emperor Sutoku took the throne; Fujiwara Tadamichi, regent for an infant emperor, held the realm, and the practical power of the palace fell to Fujiwara Tadasumi, chief of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, while Fujiwara Yorimichi, kanpaku, was the government's face in foreign and ceremonial matters. Tadasumi loved to gather power and was skilled at managing the courtiers around him, while Yorimichi was expanding fast, and the two men came to exclude each other: the tradition has it that Tadasumi repeatedly schemed to push Yorimichi aside, and in the end Yorimichi's side struck first. In the twelfth month of the third year of the Kyōan era, Minamoto no Tamemori and his son killed Tadasumi in a palace procession, and Tadasumi's head was carried to Itsukushima. That single step raised a murder in the palace into open war between regent and kanpaku. Tadamichi mustered troops in Kyoto against Yorimichi at once, broke into the Nijō residence, and Yorimichi fled, eventually taking refuge on the island behind Emperor Toba with the court's recognition; Tadamichi's pursuing force then crossed the sea. Thus a feud inside the regent's clan that might have been settled by court mediation and by the balancing of offices was escalated, because a man had been killed, into a war with real armies, a sea crossing and a struggle for a fortified position. The deeper cause lies in the fact that the two branches of the regent clan, the clerical offices and the warrior houses each wanted their own place; the jurisdictions of regent and kanpaku already overlapped, and military force was now able to decide who held the capital. That is the true background of the so-called Kafuku no Hen.
impact: 果腹之變的直接後果，是藤原賴宗在島上站穩了腳跟。忠通兵敗退走，忠實之冤未雪，攝政之位一度旁落；賴宗隨後入京執政，藤原家的兩房由此公開分道，忠通一系退居備前與陸奧一帶埋伏，賴宗一系在朝廷主政二十餘年，直到1156年保元之亂的京都夜鬥，賴宗與忠通雙雙身死——那場更大的政變，正是這次島上私鬥的放大版，也是平氏得以抬頭、平治之亂與治承三年之政變接連發生的起點。次級的影響同樣深遠：平清盛因為效忠被暗殺的忠實而捲入敗局，敗退備前、寄人籬下，卻因此保住了性命與勢力，日後反而在1156年執政，開啟平氏執政的時代；源義仲退回陸奧，以蝦夷之王的兇名在東北坐大，日後平治物語中他的種種傳說，源頭就在這次島上的失利。此外，此役在史料上還留下一份教訓：以攝政與關白之尊，最終仍要靠短兵相接與渡海登陸來解決分歧；武器、舟船與島嶼地形第一次被寫進了攝政與關白之間的勝負簿。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the Kafuku no Hen was that Fujiwara Yorimichi held his ground on the island. Tadamichi's army was defeated and withdrew, Tadasumi's grievance was not redressed, and the regency passed for a time out of Tadamichi's hands; Yorimichi entered the capital and governed, the two branches of the Fujiwara visibly split, and Tadamichi's side lay low in Bizen and in Mutsu while Yorimichi's side held the court for more than twenty years, until the night fighting in Kyoto in 1156, the Hōgen disturbance, when Yorimichi and Tadamichi both died. That larger upheaval was the magnified version of this private quarrel on the island, and the starting point of the rise of the Taira, of the Heiji war and of the war of 1180. The secondary effects were no less deep: Taira Kiyomori, having served the murdered Tadasumi, was drawn into the defeat and sent back to Bizen to live off the charity of local magnates, and that very disgrace preserved his life and his power, so that he was the one who took charge in 1156 and opened the era of Taira government. Minamoto Yoshinaka withdrew to Mutsu and grew into a feared ruler of the north-east, and the legends that gather around him in the Heiji narrative have their root in this island defeat. For the historical record there is also a lesson: even a regent and a kanpaku could not settle their differences except by closing quarters and by landing from the sea; weapons, boats and the shape of an island entered the reckoning between regent and kanpaku for the first time.
result: 結果很簡單：守方勝。賴宗以少數人馬退守嚴島巖窟，利用孤島的地形、潮汐與水源，把遠道而來的攝政大軍拖到力竭，忠通的海船在島外等不到可乘之機，終於退兵。忠實的仇沒有報，忠通失去攝政之位，兩房的裂痕從宮廷內部擴散到武人的效忠與流亡；義仲走陸奧，清盛遁備前，賴宗自此入主院中，這場戰爭也從此以果腹之變之名被後世記下。史載細節有限、諸說並存的地方主要有三處：參戰兵力的確數、決戰的具體時辰與部署，以及首級獻上的儀式細節，後世小說多有加油添醋。但大方向沒有爭議：這是一場以孤島為憑、靠地形與消耗取勝的守方戰役，也是1156年保元之亂前夜，藤原兩房用戰爭解決宮廷分歧的最後一次預演。
resultEn: The result is simple: the defence won. With a handful of men Yorimichi held the caves of Itsukushima and used the terrain, the tides and the water of the island to exhaust an attacking regent's army that had come a long way; Tadamichi's ships waited off the shore and found no opening, and at last withdrew. The murderer of Tadasumi went unpunished, Tadamichi lost the regency, and the rift between the two branches spread from the inner palace to the loyalty and flight of warriors: Yoshinaka went back to Mutsu, Kiyomori took refuge in Bizen, and Yorimichi from that point held the palace. From then on the war was remembered under the name of the Kafuku no Hen. Three things in the record are thinly attested and open to dispute: the exact numbers engaged, the precise hour and deployment of the decisive action, and the ceremonial details of the presentation of the head; later fiction has added a good deal of embroidery to all three. The broad lines are not contested. This was a defensive battle won on a lonely island by terrain and attrition, and it was the last rehearsal, before the Hōgen disturbance of 1156, of the two branches of the Fujiwara settling a dispute of the court by means of war.
